It is also Y.' mold before the anaphora begins. Also 3412 'That is the real goal.' and 3423 'motivated, reasonable, and theatrically natural... not that they are being walked through a suspicious procedure' are the same mold in the section intros.
findings.rewrite: Michael Gutenplan pointed out something I had not thought about: pre-show is also how you protect the person you are about to use.

chapter_notes: Ch26 (3283-3342): The virus/contagion framework is a strong, real idea and the epidemiology analogy is worth keeping, but almost every paragraph is built as setup-sentence, contrast-sentence, aphorism-closer. I count roughly 18 negative-parallelism constructions and 16 punch-ending paragraphs in 57 lines of prose, with paired mirrored paragraphs at 3301/3302 (low-contagion/high-contagion) and 3305/3306 (used as a prop/part of something). One punch per section is Chris; this chapter averages one per paragraph.

Ch26: 'genuinely' or 'genuine' appears six times in this chapter (3304, 3309 x3, 3312, 3326, 3332) and 'entirely' twice. 'Structural' three times. These are the model's intensifiers, not Chris's (his are 'dude', 'insane', 'so damn good', caps).

Ch26 Colin Cloud framework cards: six pull-quote cards (3288, 3295/3296, 3299, 3307/3308, 3318/3319, 3324/3325, 3329/3330) and five of them are two-sentence mirrored aphorisms in the exact 'isn't X. It's Y' / 'X protects A. Y protects B' shape as the surrounding narration. Chris should check whether these are Colin's actual words. If they are paraphrases, they currently make Colin sound like the same model voice as the body text. The em dash in the card label 'Colin Cloud — Framework' is a layout artifact (9 of the 20 em dashes in the range are these labels or the chapter header) but note the no-em-dash rule for the printed book.

Ch26: The chapter ending (3336-3342) is a drumroll: rhetorical question, tricolon of 'nothing that...', 'You are making a bet.', 'Bet carefully.', 'Start there.' Five punches in seven lines. Chris's real closers are usually one line and then he moves on.

Ch26 authentic Chris: line 3334 ('I do utilize pre-show but have learned to limit its usage as a means of reducing the amount of work required for me and my team before the show begins. Not relying on pre-show gives me more peace of mind on stage and leads to less frantic and chaotic moments') is clunky, first person, practical, and unmistakably him. Keep it as-is. Also the luggage/catching-a-flight targeting detail at 3326 and the 'parking lot comparing experiences' image at 3316 are real performer detail. The drop-cap artifact 'E / very pre-show' at 3284-3285 is a layout fragment, ignore.

Ch27 prose section (3356-3401): the most machine-dense stretch in the range. Every paragraph ends on a contrast or aphorism, several end on two or three stacked. Counted about 40 negative-parallelism constructions in 46 lines of prose (3359 alone has five, 3393 has three plus a triple anaphora). Recurring template: '[Abstract] is not X. It is Y.' with Y a single abstract noun (amplification, certainty, surgical, deadness, professionalism, architecture).

Ch27: Section headers themselves lean into the mold ('JUSTIFICATION IS NOT COSMETIC', 'WHAT STRONG PRE-SHOW ACTUALLY DOES', 'WHAT THOSE LINES ARE REALLY DOING'), which is the persuasive-authority trope ('actually', 'really') in heading form. Not flagged as findings since they are structural, but worth a pass.

Ch27 authentic Chris: the private script at 3369-3381 ('Are you capable of remembering that word?', 'Just checking, you still remember what it is, right?', 'Deal?'), the 'Oh! One more thing. Do not let me in your head' add-on at 3386, the drink-from-a-notebook toast example at 3365 (idea, not the commentary), the Broca/Exner line at 3436, and the '45 seconds' and 'heat of the moment' lines at 3454/3456 all sound like a working performer. The commentary wrapped around each of them is where the model shows up: script line, then 'That line is not rude. It is surgical.'

Ch27 line catalog (3413-3525): structural, so mostly not flagged, but the gloss column under each line is generated in one mold: 'Sounds/Feels/Makes it X, not Y' about 14 times and 'adjective, adjective, and adjective' about 6 times ('Short, mysterious, and non-accusatory', 'Modern, clean, and live-sounding', 'stable, important, and clearly on the right side of the room'). Chris's version of an annotation would be a field note: where he used it, what the spectator did. The Michael Gutenplan credits at 3441 and 3468 are good and specific; keep those.

Ch27 Gutenplan sections (3392-3396): the ideas are attributed to Michael Gutenplan but the prose is the manuscript's (contributor=false in findings). Both paragraphs close with the heaviest punch-stacks in the chapter (3393 especially). The 'Imagine... Imagine... Imagine...' anaphora at 3392 would be stronger as one real story Chris actually lived through.

Range-wide: em dashes total 20 (11 in body prose, 9 in card labels/headers). No en dashes. Chris's standing rule is zero em dashes in anything public; each of the 11 prose dashes is a reveal-dash or aside that should become a comma, period, or parentheses. The epigraph at 3527 ('The safest secret is the one they watched you fail to find.') belongs to the next section and is an aphorism formula but was not flagged since it is a deliberate epigraph.
group_verdict: This stretch reads like a model, and the Ch27 prose section (3356 to 3401) is the worst of it; the only paragraphs a reader who knows Chris would recognize as his are the clunky first-person use-case paragraph at 3334, the luggage-and-flight targeting detail at 3326, the forty-coworkers-at-a-corporate-dinner specifics at 3312, the notebook-toast idea at 3365, and the private script lines themselves (3369 to 3381, 3386). The single most damaging habit is the contrast hammer used as the default paragraph closer: 'X is not A. It is B.' with B a one-word abstract noun (amplification, certainty, surgical, deadness, professionalism, architecture), stacked two or three deep at the end of nearly every paragraph and mirrored across paired paragraphs (3305/3306, 3301/3302). Everything else (the tricolons, the 'genuinely' tic, the em-dash reveals, the repeated 'tell the truth and still sound impossible' slogan) hangs off that skeleton, so if Chris rewrites only one thing, it should be the closers: end each paragraph on the concrete detail or the field anecdote and delete the aphorism after it. Two cautions on the first reader's rewrites: several reintroduce the same pattern (3293, 3314, 3321) and two invent first-person claims that are not in the manuscript ('I have made that bet and lost it' at 3338, 'nobody has ever taken it the wrong way' at 3383); those violate the truth rule and should not be pasted unless they are actually true. Also, line 3300 sits under a 'Colin Cloud — Framework' label like the other cards, so Chris should confirm whether it is his narration or a Colin paraphrase, and the six Colin cards all share the narration's 'isn't X. It's Y' shape, which makes Colin sound like the same model as the body text.

group.label: Ch27A, Ch28 Digital Pre-show (first part)

findings.quote: Everything in this chapter so far hides the pre-show by making it forgettable — an innocent, logistical moment the participant files under nothing.
findings.why: Reveal dash followed by a polished abstraction ("files under nothing"). Chris would set this up with a colon or a plain second sentence.
findings.where: Ch27A The Pre-Show That Looks Like a Failure
findings.rewrite: Everything in this chapter so far hides the pre-show by making it forgettable: a boring, logistical moment the participant never thinks about again.
findings.verifier_reason: Verbatim. Reveal dash into a polished abstraction ("files under nothing"); dash must go under the standing rule regardless. Not the worst thing in 27A but it opens the section on the model's rhythm.

findings.quote: That is the entire method. You fail on purpose.
findings.why: On its own this is a Chris punch. The problem is density: 27A has a punch or aphorism closing nearly every paragraph (3535, 3537, 3542, 3543), so this one reads as the first beat of a model rhythm.
findings.verifier_reason: Verbatim, but this is the one punch in 27A that reads like Chris talking ("You fail on purpose."). The density problem is real and is captured by the other 27A findings; this is the line to keep when the rest are stripped.

findings.quote: They did not watch you succeed. They watched you try and come up empty. Nobody guards the memory of a thing that did not work.
findings.why: Two mirrored negative sentences and then a quotable aphorism with an abstract subject ("Nobody guards the memory"). Classic model contrast hammer.
findings.rewrite: They watched you try and come up empty. Nobody thinks twice about a thing that didn't work.
findings.verifier_reason: Verbatim. Two mirrored negatives then a free-floating aphorism with an abstract subject, inside a paragraph that already has "Here there is nothing to trace." This is the contrast hammer at full swing.

findings.quote: only an earlier failure, which makes the later hit feel like something you finally broke through to, not something you arranged.
findings.why: Reveal dash plus a tailing "X, not Y" negation. Second contrast device in the same paragraph.
findings.verifier_reason: Verbatim. Dash reveal plus tailing "X, not Y" as the second contrast device in the same paragraph. Chris would end this with a colon or a plain clause.

findings.quote: They are not surprised when you circle back, because you told them you might. They are not suspicious, because in their own experience you genuinely did not get it the first time. And they are quietly invested — they want to see
findings.why: "They are not... They are not... And they are" triple with "genuinely" and "quietly" as the adverb tics, capped by a dash reveal. Every model tell in one sentence run.
findings.rewrite: When you circle back they aren't surprised, you told them you might. They aren't suspicious either, because as far as they know you really didn't get it the first time. And now they want to see if you can.
findings.verifier_reason: Verbatim. "They are not... They are not... And they are" with both adverb tics (genuinely, quietly) and a dash reveal in one run. Unmistakable.

findings.quote: You have turned the one person most able to expose you into the one person rooting hardest for the miracle.
findings.why: Mirrored "the one person... into the one person" aphorism used as a paragraph closer directly after the anaphora run.
findings.rewrite: The one person who could bust you is now the one person pulling for you.
findings.verifier_reason: Verbatim. Mirrored "the one person... into the one person" closer landing directly on top of the anaphora run. Two closers in one paragraph is the model's stacking habit.

findings.quote: That sentence quietly tells the participant which moment you are reaching back to, so they lock onto the earlier experience — while the audience hears nothing but a mind reader widening his claim.
findings.why: "quietly" tic plus a dash-pivot to a stylized abstraction ("a mind reader widening his claim"). The practical content is good; the phrasing is the model's.
findings.verifier_reason: Verbatim. "quietly" plus a dash pivot to a stylized phrase ("a mind reader widening his claim"). The practical content (the callback line, the word tonight, the lion) is Chris and should stay; only the framing sentence is model.

findings.quote: The rest of pre-show works by making the secret moment vanish. This works by making it visible and harmless. Both leave the participant able to tell the exact truth about what happened and still have it sound impossible.
findings.why: Mirrored two-sentence contrast (vanish / visible) then a third sentence resolving them. Tidy symmetrical reasoning that reads engineered.
findings.verifier_reason: Verbatim. Not strictly chiasmus, but a balanced vanish/visible pair resolved by a third symmetrical sentence. Tidy engineered logic rather than a person explaining.

findings.quote: Let them say that. It is the best testimony you could ask for.
findings.why: Two-beat closer immediately followed by a standalone aphorism line (3543). Punch on punch.
findings.verifier_reason: Verbatim. Two-beat closer immediately followed by the standalone aphorism at 3543. Punch on punch; the participant quote before it is the human beat.

findings.quote: Fail first, and the miracle has no past for them to search.
findings.why: Standalone one-line aphorism as a section ender, with an abstract noun (the miracle) as agent. This is the model writing a pull quote, not Chris talking.
findings.rewrite: Fail first. Then there is nothing for them to go back and find.
findings.verifier_reason: Verbatim. Standalone one-line section ender with "the miracle" as an abstract agent. This is a pull quote, not something said on stage or in a text.

findings.quote: "The most powerful thing you can know about a person is the thing they never thought to hide."
findings.why: Unattributed epigraph in the "X is the Y" formula. If this is Chris's own line it should be signed; if the model wrote it, it is a manufactured quote.
findings.verifier_reason: Verbatim (straight quotes in source). Epigraph, so structural, but the wording is the "X is the Y" aphorism formula and it is unattributed. Either sign it or cut it.

findings.quote: You do not know the performer. You were not given any kind of intake form. You did not stop at a registration table and fill out a card. Nobody has spoken to you since you sat down.
findings.why: Four negative sentences in a row ("You do not... You were not... You did not... Nobody"). The scene is a good idea; the stacked negation is the model's rhythm.
findings.rewrite: You've never met the performer. No intake form, no registration card, nobody has said a word to you since you sat down.
findings.verifier_reason: Verbatim. Four consecutive negations to set a scene. The second-person scene is a Chris structure; the stacked "You do not / You were not / You did not / Nobody" is the model's rhythm.

findings.quote: you recently had a birthday — and not just that you had one, but how old you turned, and that the celebration was small
findings.why: Dash reveal plus "not just X but Y" escalation. Note the rest of this paragraph ("Excited, but skeptical, you agree. After a few questions about your life...") reads like a hand edit and should stay.
findings.verifier_reason: Verbatim. Dash reveal plus "not just that... but" escalation, in a paragraph that also runs "He says / He says / He pauses." The clunky "After a few questions about your life and how you tend to categorize information in your mind." is a hand edit and should stay.

findings.quote: You do not ask how he knew. You already feel like it would be the wrong question. Whatever category of person this man is, it is one you have not encountered before.
findings.why: Three short declaratives building to a closer, then another closer paragraph right after (3562). Staccato drama.
findings.verifier_reason: Verbatim. Three staccato declaratives building to a closer, immediately followed by another closer paragraph. Cinematic staccato drama per taxonomy section 31.

findings.quote: That feeling, that specific, slightly disorienting certainty that you have been seen, is not an accident. The raw material that made it possible was gathered long before the performer stepped into the room.
findings.why: "is not an accident" tailing negation followed by the cinematic reveal sentence. This is the model's standard scene-to-thesis transition.
findings.rewrite: That feeling of being seen didn't happen by luck. The performer did the work days before he walked in.
findings.verifier_reason: Verbatim. Appositive restatement ("That feeling, that specific...") plus "is not an accident" tailing negation plus the cinematic reveal sentence. Standard model scene-to-thesis pivot.

findings.quote: Not quite discomfort. Something more like the particular alertness that comes when a subject you have already privately wrestled with gets named out loud.

findings.quote: These are not private acts. They are records of a person as they have chosen to present themselves to the world around them, however casually or thoughtlessly that choice was made. Reading those records is not surveillance.

findings.verifier_reason: Verbatim. "These are not X. They are Y." then a tailing "is not surveillance" closer, on top of a three-sentence "The person who / The person whose / The name in" anaphora opening the paragraph.

findings.quote: The line is not between researching and not researching. The line is between using what exists in the public record and weaponizing what you find.

findings.verifier_reason: Verbatim. "The line is not X. The line is Y." is the exact template the brief names.

group_verdict: This stretch reads like a model with Chris spliced in. The human beats are easy to spot because they are the messy ones: the TJ Tana green fridge paragraph (BINGO!, WOW!, TINY, "It's all gold if you know how to be creative"), the SOCOM credential, the Brookings practical notes (three people, the seed, the word tonight, the lion), the DelGaudio reference, the grammar slips at 3560 and 3594, and the "Inversely, people who have no choice but to be there" sentence. Everything around those beats runs on one engine, and that engine is the single most damaging habit here: the paragraph-closing aphorism built on a negative parallelism. "The line is not X. The line is Y." "The mechanism is different. The ethics are structurally identical." "The information is the foundation. You are the method." "Still valuable. A different kind of valuable." "It does not feel like a trick. It feels like being known." It lands at the end of nearly every paragraph in 27A and the entire ethics section (3566 to 3585), so the reader gets a deck of pull quotes instead of a working mentalist explaining how he does pre-show. Chris's real punch is one short line after a long paragraph and then he moves on; here the punch is the paragraph. Fix strategy: keep the specifics and the method notes untouched, strip the closers down to one per section, kill every dash, and rewrite the ethics section from the calibration sample at 3564 rather than polishing the model's version of it.

group.label: Ch28 Digital Pre-show (rest)

findings.quote: This is the category where the highest-impact Tier One material lives
findings.why: The "where X lives" formula is a model aphorism shape; it recurs at line 3758 ("where the most powerful mentalism lives"), so it is a habit, not a one-off. The sentence right after it ("I have some notes about this that I will share later on") is Chris.
findings.where: Ch28 Digital Pre-show, Obituary and Family Member Intelligence
findings.rewrite: This is where the best Tier One material comes from, so it is worth learning the search cold.
findings.verifier_reason: Verbatim. The "where X lives" formula appears about 15 times across the manuscript and once at 3622 just fifty lines earlier ("This is where most of the Tier One material lives"), so it is a real template. On its own here it is a tic, and the next sentence ("I have some notes about this that I will share later on") is Chris. Low.

findings.quote: which appear with genuine frequency and land with particular weight in performance
findings.why: "genuine frequency" and "particular weight" are inflation adverbials that say nothing a number or example would not say better. "genuine frequency" is reused verbatim at line 3614, just above this range, which marks it as a model phrase.
findings.where: Ch28 Digital Pre-show, Obituary and Family Member Intelligence
findings.rewrite: Deceased siblings and kids show up more often than you would expect, and they hit hard in a show, so the search is the same but add detail:
findings.verifier_reason: Verbatim, and "appear with genuine frequency" is confirmed to repeat word for word at 3614. Two inflation adverbials in one subordinate clause where Chris would give a number or a story. Medium.

findings.quote: Use these with care. This material exists at the far edge of what performance should touch.
findings.why: Two-sentence paragraph that exists only to land an aphoristic closer. "the far edge of what performance should touch" is quotable-line phrasing rather than an instruction.
findings.where: Ch28 Digital Pre-show, Obituary and Family Member Intelligence
findings.rewrite: Be careful with these. This is about as far as I think a show should ever go, and I will get into the rules below.
findings.verifier_reason: "Use these with care" is Chris. "This material exists at the far edge of what performance should touch" is a quotable closer with an abstract noun doing the acting. One punch per section is his; this one is model wording, not model density. Medium.

findings.quote: A birthday, a work anniversary, a promotion: these appear on other people’s timelines even when the subject’s own account is locked.
findings.why: Colon-fronted triple fragment used as a rhetorical setup. Same shape appears at 3696 ("a name in a high school honor roll, a youth sports photograph with a caption, a family business story") and 3714 ("a social media post, a news mention, a public record").
findings.where: Ch28 Digital Pre-show, The Social Graph
findings.rewrite: Their friends post about their birthday, their promotion, their work anniversary, and none of that is locked down just because the person's own profile is.
findings.verifier_reason: Colon-fronted triple is real and it does cluster with 3696 and 3714, but the paragraph is short, instructional, and the device is used once. Only worth flagging because of the cluster. Low, not medium.

findings.quote: A family member’s name that appears in an obituary and in a tagged Instagram post is solid.
findings.why: Three parallel sentences in a row ending "is solid... is solid... is soft", followed by an "impression rather than a statement" contrast. The rule is good; the drumbeat delivery is the model's.
findings.rewrite: If a birthday shows up on Facebook and in an Instagram post, you are good. Same with a family name that appears in an obituary and a tagged post. If you only found it once and cannot back it up, treat it as soft and deliver it as an impression, not a fact.
findings.verifier_reason: Verbatim. "is solid... is solid... is soft" then "impression rather than a statement" is the drumbeat-then-contrast build. The same shape recurs at 3720 ("gets delivered... gets delivered"), which the first reader missed, so it is a habit in this section. Medium.

findings.quote: This is not primarily a legal or ethical matter, don’t worry. It is a performance security matter.
findings.why: Textbook "It is not X. It is Y." hammer. The "don't worry" aside reads like a Chris insertion into a model sentence, which makes the seam visible.
findings.where: Ch28 Digital Pre-show, Note on Search History
findings.rewrite: This is not a legal thing, do not worry. It is show security.
findings.verifier_reason: Textbook "This is not X. It is Y." and the "don't worry" aside shows exactly where Chris touched a model sentence. The seam is the tell. High.

findings.quote: Protect the intelligence because the intelligence protects the effect.
findings.why: Mirrored A-B / B-A aphorism used as a paragraph closer. Pure quotable-line construction; Chris would end on the practical instruction, not a slogan.
findings.where: Ch28 Digital Pre-show, Note on Search History
findings.rewrite: The person most likely to blow it is the nice event contact who borrows your laptop before the show. Keep the research in an incognito window and close it.
findings.verifier_reason: Full chiasmus as a paragraph closer. Nobody says this out loud; it is slogan construction. High.

findings.quote: the discipline is documentation.
findings.why: Abstract noun equated to abstract noun as a punch. The sentence before it is a long qualifier chain that exists to set up this three-word landing.
findings.where: Ch28 Digital Pre-show, The Build: Constructing a Dossier
findings.rewrite: Once you have your two or three targets (more than that only if the whole show is built around this), write it all down.
findings.verifier_reason: A 30-word qualifier chain ("ideally no more than... unless the show is specifically designed around...") built to land on a three-word abstract equation. Chris would say "write it down." Medium.

findings.quote: How you deliver intelligence is as important as the intelligence itself.
findings.why: Mirrored-noun opener ("X is as important as X itself") followed by a "gathered rather than perceived" contrast at the end of the same paragraph. Two rhetorical devices in a four-sentence paragraph.
findings.where: Ch28 Digital Pre-show, The Delivery Protocol
findings.rewrite: The biggest mistake is dumping everything you know at once. Stack reveal on reveal and each one gets weaker, and the sharp people in the room start to figure out you looked it up.
findings.verifier_reason: Mirrored-noun opener plus "gathered rather than perceived" closer in a four-sentence paragraph. The middle content (over-delivering, stacking reveals) is fine. Medium.

findings.quote: one detail early, treated lightly; one detail mid-show, treated with more weight; the Tier One detail held for the moment of maximum context. The audience experiences not one reveal but a building pattern
findings.why: Semicolon-built three-beat list, then a "not one X but a Y" pivot, then a "happening to them... rather than shown at them" contrast to close. Three model devices stacked in one paragraph.
findings.where: Ch28 Digital Pre-show, The Delivery Protocol
findings.rewrite: Space it out. One light detail early, something heavier in the middle, and the big one when the room is ready for it. It should feel like something is building on them, not like a list is being read at them.
findings.verifier_reason: "The superior approach is paced deployment" then a semicolon tricolon, then "not one reveal but a building pattern", then "happening to them... rather than something being shown at them". Three devices in two sentences. High.

findings.quote: You are not probing or fishing. You simply know. The person who already knows does not announce that they know. They simply tell you.
findings.why: Negative parallelism, a two-word punch, then a mirrored aphorism, then a repeat of "simply" as a closer. Every sentence is a landing; nothing is doing setup work.
findings.where: Ch28 Digital Pre-show, The Delivery Protocol
findings.rewrite: Do not explain the method or even hint at it. You are not fishing. You already know, so say it the way someone who knows would say it.
findings.verifier_reason: Four consecutive landing sentences with no setup, and "simply" twice. "The person who already knows does not announce that they know" is pure aphorism. High.

findings.quote: The caption on the post, a photograph of the two of them from years earlier, was quiet and direct. She had clearly written it for herself rather than for an audience.
findings.why: "quiet" is a model tic (it recurs at 3754, "a quiet kind of authority"), and "for herself rather than for an audience" is a contrast hammer. The rest of the paragraph (Patricia, forty-two, floral arrangements) is authentic, specific Chris material.
findings.where: Ch28 Digital Pre-show, Chris Michael's Take
findings.rewrite: The caption was short and honest. You could tell she wrote it for herself. It mentioned that she and her mom used to make floral arrangements for friends.
findings.verifier_reason: Story specifics are Chris (Patricia, forty-two, floral arrangements) but "was quiet and direct" and "for herself rather than for an audience" are model description plus contrast hammer laid over a real anecdote. "quiet" recurs at 3754. Medium.

findings.quote: No names. No specifics.
findings.why: Two-fragment stack inside a first-person story that is otherwise Chris. On its own it is fine; it clusters with the model-cadence closer at 3730 and the "quiet" tic at 3727.
findings.where: Ch28 Digital Pre-show, Chris Michael's Take
findings.verifier_reason: Drop. "No names. No specifics." is a short clarifying punch after a long dictated-feeling sentence, which is exactly the rhythm Chris's own voice profile describes. Used once in the Take, it reads as him. The Take's real problem is 3730, not this line.

findings.quote: That is the use of intelligence that I believe in. Not to shock. Not to demonstrate access. To see the person in front of you with enough specificity that the seeing itself becomes the gift. The method disappears because the experience is real and heartfelt.
findings.why: "Not to... Not to... To..." anaphora, a "the seeing itself becomes the gift" aphorism, and a causal-mirror closer, all stacked on the best story in the chapter. The story earns its ending; the model overwrote it.
findings.where: Ch28 Digital Pre-show, Chris Michael's Take
findings.rewrite: That is how I want to use this stuff. Not to shock her or show off that I can find things. I wanted her to feel seen, and when it is that specific and that kind, nobody in the room is thinking about method.
findings.verifier_reason: "Not to shock. Not to demonstrate access. To see..." anaphora, then "the seeing itself becomes the gift", then a causal mirror. The story earned a plain ending and got a monologue. "real and heartfelt" may be a Chris insertion but it does not rescue the paragraph. High.

findings.quote: This chapter would be incomplete without being explicit about the territory it does not endorse.
findings.why: Announces that the section is about to say something instead of saying it. "the territory it does not endorse" is abstract-noun phrasing for "the stuff you should not do."
findings.rewrite: Here is what I will not do with this, and what I do not think you should either.
findings.verifier_reason: Announces the section instead of starting it, and "the territory it does not endorse" is abstraction where Chris would just say what he will not do. Medium.

findings.quote: can be used in ways that are coercive, manipulative, or genuinely harmful. Information gathered about a person without their consent, deployed to pressure them, embarrass them, or destabilize them in front of an audience they cannot leave, crosses from performance into something else entirely.
findings.why: Two rule-of-three lists back to back, a "genuinely" intensifier, and an "into something else entirely" closer that gestures at a category without naming it. The phrase "an audience they cannot leave" is the one real image and it is buried.
findings.rewrite: The same searches can be used to pressure or embarrass someone in front of a room they cannot walk out of. At that point it is not a show anymore.
findings.verifier_reason: Back-to-back tricolons ("coercive, manipulative, or genuinely harmful" / "pressure them, embarrass them, or destabilize them"), "genuinely", and "into something else entirely" as a closer that names nothing. High.

findings.quote: The general shape of “you’ve had a difficult year” is different from naming the person they lost. The first acknowledges. The second intrudes.
findings.why: Mirrored two-word fragments as a paragraph closer ("The first X. The second Y.") is one of the most recognizable model cadences in the book. The rule is important enough that it should sound like Chris saying it.
findings.rewrite: Saying "you have had a hard year" is one thing. Saying her mom's name is a completely different thing, and you do not get to do it.
findings.verifier_reason: "The first acknowledges. The second intrudes." is one of the most recognizable model cadences in the whole book, and it lands on the most important rule in the chapter. High.

findings.quote: The implicit contract of pre-show work is that you are surfacing what the subject has, in some sense, already put into the world.
findings.why: Abstract framing ("the implicit contract") plus a hedge ("in some sense") the CLAUDE.md voice rules explicitly forbid. Earlier in the same paragraph a three-item list ("a mutual contact sharing private information, a private message, a non-public professional record") does the tricolon thing again.
findings.rewrite: If they did not put it out there themselves, you do not get to use it. That is the deal.
findings.verifier_reason: "The implicit contract" plus the "in some sense" hedge the project voice rules forbid, preceded by another colon-free tricolon ("a mutual contact sharing private information, a private message, a non-public professional record"). Medium.

findings.quote: If someone looks distressed rather than astonished, you adjust. You offer a social door. You give them a way to breathe.
findings.why: "rather than" contrast then three short "You X" sentences in a row. The content (social door, barn door, Chapter 15) is Chris's framework; the staccato delivery is the model's.
findings.rewrite: If they look upset instead of amazed, you change course right there and give them a way out. Same barn door language from Chapter 15, and it matters more here than anywhere because it is their life, not a card.
findings.verifier_reason: "distressed rather than astonished" then three staccato "You X" sentences, the last of which ("You give them a way to breathe") is quotable-line phrasing. The framework content is Chris; the delivery is not. Medium.

findings.quote: This method is powerful precisely because it is not theatrical. It feels real because the information is real.
findings.why: "precisely because it is not" plus a mirrored "feels real because... is real" line. Two aphorisms in a row before Chris's own closer ("For the sake of all of us performers, please handle it accordingly"), which reads authentic and should be kept.
findings.rewrite: It works because there is no trick frame around it. The information is real, so it feels real. Please be careful with it, for all of us.
findings.verifier_reason: "powerful precisely because it is not" plus "feels real because the information is real", two aphorisms in a row immediately before Chris's own authentic closer. The contrast with "For the sake of all of us performers, please handle it accordingly" makes the model lines more visible, not less. High.

findings.quote: A file on your phone works. A paper note in your inside pocket works.
findings.why: Parallel "X works. Y works." pair, and the paragraph then closes on "Your pre-show preparation is invisible by design", an "X by design" aphorism closer.
findings.rewrite: Notes go on your phone or on a paper in your jacket pocket, not on a screen someone can glance at before the show.
findings.verifier_reason: The "works. ... works." pair on its own is borderline practical, but the paragraph ends on "Your pre-show preparation is invisible by design", an aphorism closer, and that is what pushes it to medium.

findings.quote: watch blink rate, watch postural shift, and watch the hands. The ethics framework established in Chapter 38 applies here with particular force. This method operates entirely within the domain of consent and context
findings.why: Anaphoric triple ("watch... watch... watch"), then "with particular force" and "operates entirely within the domain of" inflation in a cross-reference note that should be plain.
findings.rewrite: For reading how the reveal is landing in real time, use the cortisol window stuff from Chapter 5: blink rate, posture, hands. And read Chapter 38 before you try this in a high stakes room.
findings.verifier_reason: "watch... watch... watch", "with particular force", "operates entirely within the domain of consent and context". A cross-reference note should be the plainest prose in the chapter and instead it is inflated. Medium.

findings.quote: when it works correctly it produces the kind of moment that performers spend entire careers trying to build.
findings.why: Importance inflation before the content arrives. Paired with the opener "more powerful in combination than in isolation", the paragraph is two sentences of hype and one of setup. The final sentence about gauging whether a topic is appropriate reads like Chris and should stay.
findings.where: Ch28 Digital Pre-show, Combining Standard Pre-show with Digital Pre-show
findings.rewrite: Everything in these two chapters works better together. But one specific combo is the best moment I know how to build: a peeked name plus a fast search in the window before the reveal.
findings.verifier_reason: "more powerful in combination than in isolation" then "the kind of moment that performers spend entire careers trying to build". Chris hypes, but his hype is specific and physical; this is abstract importance inflation. The final sentence about gauging appropriateness is Chris and should stay. Medium.

findings.quote: Here is the structure in plain terms.
findings.why: One-line announcement paragraph. Clusters with "What matters is what you do next" at 3751 and "The name comes last" at 3755: three one-liner signposts in one section.
findings.where: Ch28 Digital Pre-show, Combining Standard Pre-show with Digital Pre-show
findings.verifier_reason: Drop. "Here is the structure in plain terms." is a direct reader instruction, which the voice rules list as one of Chris's own form-breaking moves. Neutral wording, no rhetorical device. The one-liner cluster in this section is carried by 3751 and 3755, not this line.

findings.quote: The framing is warm and deliberate. You are not asking for a random name. You are asking for someone who matters
findings.why: "deliberate" tic plus a "You are not X. You are Y." hammer. The setup for the exercise is good; the model shape on top is unmistakable.
findings.where: Ch28 Digital Pre-show, Combining Standard Pre-show with Digital Pre-show
findings.rewrite: You are not asking for a random name. You want someone who mattered to them, so before anything happens they are already in it emotionally.
findings.verifier_reason: "warm and deliberate" then "You are not asking for a random name. You are asking for someone who matters". The hammer is unmistakable and "deliberate" is a tic word that recurs at 3756. High.

findings.quote: That conversation tells you the emotional temperature. It tells you whether the room is ready for weight or whether something lighter is more appropriate. It also, frequently, tells you more than you asked.
findings.why: Three consecutive "tells you" sentences, followed by "genuine warmth" and a "This is not meant to be a method. Instead..." negative parallelism earlier in the same paragraph. "File that." at the end is a Chris-style punch and reads fine.
findings.where: Ch28 Digital Pre-show, Combining Standard Pre-show with Digital Pre-show
findings.rewrite: That conversation tells you if the room can handle something heavy tonight or if you should keep it light. And people almost always tell you more than you asked. They will say who it was, that people in the room knew them, that they are doing okay. File that.
findings.verifier_reason: Three "tells you" sentences in a row, "genuine warmth", and "This is not meant to be a method. Instead..." earlier in the same paragraph. "File that." at the end reads as Chris and can stay. High for the paragraph.

findings.quote: What matters is what you do next.
findings.why: Persuasive-authority closer that announces importance instead of delivering it. The paragraph is three sentences and two of them are throat clearing.
findings.where: Ch28 Digital Pre-show, Combining Standard Pre-show with Digital Pre-show
findings.rewrite: Now you peek the name. How to peek is covered in plenty of other books. The interesting part is the next fifteen minutes.
findings.verifier_reason: One-line importance closer. The paragraph has three sentences and only "Now you peek the name" does any work. Medium.

findings.quote: You have a name. You have a surname. You have the context from your earlier conversation. You have five, ten, maybe fifteen minutes to conduct your research.
findings.why: Four "You have" sentences in a row as a paragraph opener. The rest of the paragraph (obituary, newspaper, property record) is useful and mostly clean.
findings.where: Ch28 Digital Pre-show, Combining Standard Pre-show with Digital Pre-show
findings.rewrite: So now you have a full name and the context from earlier, and maybe ten or fifteen minutes. That is enough to run it through everything in this chapter.
findings.verifier_reason: Four "You have" openers with a rising "five, ten, maybe fifteen" flourish. Chris burst-writes short lines, but not four identical frames in a row. The rest of the paragraph is useful. Medium.

findings.quote: Now you are not performing a name reveal. This has become something more.
findings.why: One-line paragraph built entirely from "not X. Y." with a vague "something more" payoff. Nothing concrete, pure cadence.
findings.where: Ch28 Digital Pre-show, Combining Standard Pre-show with Digital Pre-show
findings.rewrite: At this point you are not doing a name reveal anymore. You have a whole person.
findings.verifier_reason: A whole paragraph that is one "not X. Y." with "something more" as the payoff. Nothing concrete, all cadence. High.

findings.quote: You describe the relationship not as information but as impression, the sense that this was someone who expressed love through action rather than words, or who built things, or who carried a quiet kind of authority that did not require announcement.
findings.why: "not as X but as Y", then "action rather than words", then a rule-of-three of portrait types ending on the "quiet kind of authority" tic. Four devices in one sentence.
findings.where: Ch28 Digital Pre-show, Combining Standard Pre-show with Digital Pre-show
findings.rewrite: You do not read it like a fact sheet. You give the feel of the person: someone who showed love by doing things instead of saying them, or someone who built stuff, or the kind of person everyone listened to without them ever raising their voice.
findings.verifier_reason: "not as information but as impression", "action rather than words", a triple of portrait types, and "a quiet kind of authority that did not require announcement" in a single sentence. High.

findings.quote: You are using the biographical material you found as the architecture and your behavioral read of the participant as the texture. The two together produce something that feels like genuine perception.
findings.why: "architecture" and "texture" as metaphor pair, then "genuine" again. The two sentences that follow ("You might not even mention that they have passed... Perhaps you can let the audience tell you this") read like Chris's own addition and are the best part of the paragraph.
findings.where: Ch28 Digital Pre-show, Combining Standard Pre-show with Digital Pre-show
findings.rewrite: The facts you found are the skeleton. What you read off the person in front of you is everything else. Put them together and it feels like you actually see them.
findings.verifier_reason: Architecture/texture metaphor pair and "genuine perception" are model, but the paragraph then breaks into a looser Chris register ("You might not even mention... Perhaps you can let the audience tell you this"). The stacked-device sentence before it (index 29) is the real offender; this pair is medium.

findings.quote: The name comes last.
findings.why: One-line paragraph used as a dramatic beat, immediately followed by "That is the crucial structural decision." This is the manufactured-punchline pattern: a fragment, then a paragraph explaining why the fragment was profound.
findings.where: Ch28 Digital Pre-show, Combining Standard Pre-show with Digital Pre-show
findings.verifier_reason: "The name comes last." as a one-line paragraph is exactly the long-then-short rhythm Chris's voice doc prescribes, so the line itself is defensible. What makes it read as manufactured is the next paragraph opening "That is the crucial structural decision", which is already flagged at index 32. Keep as low only so the pair is visible in review.

findings.quote: That is the crucial structural decision. Everything you have said before the name, every detail, every impression, every piece of the portrait you have built, has been delivered without proof. The audience wants to believe it. The participant wants to believe it.
findings.why: "crucial" (taxonomy word), an "every... every... every" triple, then a mirrored "wants to believe it" pair, then "deliberately". This paragraph is the densest model cadence in the range.
findings.where: Ch28 Digital Pre-show, Combining Standard Pre-show with Digital Pre-show
findings.rewrite: Save the name for last. Everything before it, the job, the city, who they were, you deliver with no proof at all, and the whole room is leaning in wanting it to be true.
findings.verifier_reason: "crucial", an "every... every... every" triple, "wants to believe it" mirrored twice, and "deliberately". The densest single paragraph in the range; it also contains two more mirrors the first reader did not quote (see missed). High.

findings.quote: When the name arrives, it does not function as the reveal. It functions as the confirmation of everything that came before it. It is the moment the participant understands that all of it was real, not just the final word.
findings.why: "does not function as X. It functions as Y." followed by a "not just" tail, then a closing sentence built on a proof-at-end vs proof-at-beginning mirror. Three contrast hammers in four sentences.
findings.where: Ch28 Digital Pre-show, Combining Standard Pre-show with Digital Pre-show
findings.rewrite: Then the name lands and it confirms all of it at once. They realize none of it was a guess. That hits way harder than leading with the name and then trying to add details after.
findings.verifier_reason: "does not function as X. It functions as Y." then a "not just" tail, in a paragraph that already has the anchor/anchor and proof/proof mirrors. High.

findings.quote: This is the difference between a name reveal and an experience. The name reveal says: I know this. The portrait followed by the name says: I saw this person. I saw what they meant to you. And here is the proof that I am not guessing.
findings.why: "This is the difference between X and Y" frame, then mirrored "says: / says:" constructions, then an "I saw... I saw..." anaphora, then a punch closer. Whole paragraph is rhetorical scaffolding.
findings.where: Ch28 Digital Pre-show, Combining Standard Pre-show with Digital Pre-show
findings.rewrite: A name reveal says I know this. The portrait and then the name says I saw who this person was to you. Big difference.
findings.verifier_reason: "This is the difference between X and Y", mirrored "says: / says:", "I saw... I saw...", then a punch. Entirely rhetorical scaffolding with no new instruction. High.

findings.quote: Warmth without specificity is cold reading. Specificity without warmth is a demonstration. Together they are something that has no clean category, which is exactly where the most powerful mentalism lives.
findings.why: Mirrored A-without-B / B-without-A aphorism, then a "where X lives" formula closer. Earlier in the same paragraph, "each method fills a gap the other leaves open" is another mirror. This is the most quotable and least Chris paragraph in the section.
findings.where: Ch28 Digital Pre-show, Combining Standard Pre-show with Digital Pre-show
findings.rewrite: Standard pre-show gives you the feel of the person. Digital gives you the facts. You need both. Facts alone is a demo. Feel alone is cold reading.
findings.verifier_reason: Full A-without-B / B-without-A chiasmus, then "has no clean category, which is exactly where the most powerful mentalism lives", the book-wide "where X lives" template. The most quotable and least Chris paragraph in the range. High.

findings.quote: The name is not the destination. The name is the key that opens the file. What you do with the file is the performance.
findings.why: "X is not the Y. X is the Z." followed by an "X is the performance" abstract-noun punch. Section ends on three consecutive aphorisms after "The practical rule is this" signposting.
findings.where: Ch28 Digital Pre-show, Combining Standard Pre-show with Digital Pre-show
findings.rewrite: Rule: if you peek a name, that is the start of your research, not the end. The name gets you the file. The file is the show.
findings.verifier_reason: "The practical rule is this." signpost, then "X is not the Y. X is the Z. What you do with the Z is the performance." Three consecutive aphorisms to close the chapter body. High.

findings.quote: The reveal that requires no explanation is the one that was built correctly from the beginning.
findings.why: Section-closing epigraph line after the ornament. It is structural, so it will get a pass if every chapter has one, but the wording ("built correctly from the beginning") is generic-closer phrasing that could end any chapter in any book.
findings.rewrite: If you built it right from the start, nobody asks how.
findings.verifier_reason: Every chapter in the book ends with an epigraph line after the ornament (verified: "Design the memory, and you design the experience.", "Salience is not what you show. It is what they cannot ignore."), so the slot is structural. The wording here is generic enough to close any chapter, which is the only reason to keep it. Low, not medium.

findings.quote: From the arc of an act to the architecture of a career.
findings.why: False-range "from X to Y" plus the "architecture of" aphorism formula from the taxonomy, in a Part divider blurb. Structural, but the wording is machine-y and it is the first thing the reader sees in Part Four.
findings.rewrite: Show structure, scripting, and how to build a full performance from a single act up to a whole career.
findings.verifier_reason: Part divider blurb, structural. "From the arc of an act to the architecture of a career" is a false-range plus alliteration flourish, though "architecture" is a book motif rather than a taxonomy tic in this manuscript. Worth a glance because it is the first line of Part Four; not worth more than low.

findings.quote: The name is the proof, and proof delivered at the end of a sequence of true things hits with a force that proof delivered at the beginning can never produce.
findings.why: Mirrored proof-at-the-end versus proof-at-the-beginning aphorism used as the closer of the densest paragraph in the range. The first reader mentioned it in a why but never quoted it, so it is not greppable from their list.
findings.where: Ch28 Digital Pre-show, Combining Standard Pre-show with Digital Pre-show
findings.rewrite: The name is the proof. Give it at the end and it lands ten times harder than if you had led with it.

findings.quote: But belief requires an anchor, and you have withheld the anchor deliberately.
findings.why: Anadiplosis (anchor... anchor) plus the "deliberately" tic, sitting between the "wants to believe it" pair and the "does not function as" hammer. Distinct quote, same paragraph.
findings.where: Ch28 Digital Pre-show, Combining Standard Pre-show with Digital Pre-show
findings.rewrite: They want it to be true but they have nothing to hang it on yet, and that is on purpose.

findings.quote: A piece of information you found in three independently confirming sources gets delivered with full certainty. A detail you found in one source that you could not corroborate gets delivered as a question or a soft statement
findings.why: Same "X gets delivered... Y gets delivered..." drumbeat the reader flagged at 3709, in the dossier section they called clean. Two parallel 20-word sentences with identical frames. The example script that follows ("I'm getting something connected to the name... Sarah?") is fine.
findings.where: Ch28 Digital Pre-show, The Build: Constructing a Dossier
